provenance: Written 2026-09-23 from Ceph option defaults at v20.2.4, docs.ceph.com tentacle pages (mclock, network, erasure-code, crimson), Rook v1.20.7 docs, ceph-csi docs and source.

evals.name: nvme-iops-low
evals.prompt: New Rook cluster on Squid 19.2.6, 6 nodes, each with 4 Gen4 NVMe drives that do ~700k random 4k write IOPS raw. fio on an RBD PVC tops out way lower than I'd expect and recovery also feels throttled. ceph config show osd.0 osd_mclock_max_capacity_iops_ssd returns 21500. What's going on and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: mClock bench exceeded the 80000 SSD threshold, fell back to 21500 default; measure per-OSD capacity with fio and set osd_mclock_max_capacity_iops_ssd per OSD.
assertions: Explains that 21500 is the default fallback because the OSD bench result exceeded the SSD sanity threshold (80000 IOPS) and was discarded
Recommends measuring real device capacity (e.g. fio) and setting osd_mclock_max_capacity_iops_ssd explicitly per OSD
Notes the value is per OSD / must be checked on every OSD

evals.name: separate-cluster-network
evals.prompt: Designing a new Rook-Ceph cluster: 5 nodes, 2x25GbE per node bonded. Colleague insists we MUST have a separate cluster network for replication or performance will be terrible. Is that true in 2026? And if we do want isolation, host networking or Multus?
evals.expected_output: Separate cluster network optional; docs say public-only works fine at 25GE+; Multus with macvlan+whereabouts for isolation; host network trades isolation for latency.
assertions: States a separate cluster network is optional, not required, especially at 25GbE or faster
Explains host networking avoids pod-network latency but provides no isolation
Recommends Multus with the macvlan CNI (and whereabouts IPAM) if isolation is wanted

evals.name: fast-ec-existing-pool
evals.prompt: We just upgraded to Tentacle 20.2.4. Our big RBD data pool is EC 4+2 with ec_overwrites, created on Reef with default settings. I read Tentacle has 'fast EC'. Should I just flip it on for the existing pool? Any gotchas?
evals.expected_output: allow_ec_optimizations is irreversible; stripe_unit fixed at creation, old 4K default gains less, recommend 16K; consider creating a new pool; 20.2.0 crash-loop report; test first.
assertions: Names the pool flag allow_ec_optimizations
States that enabling it is irreversible for the pool
Explains stripe_unit is fixed at pool creation and that the old 4K default benefits less than 16K (so a new pool may be better)
Recommends testing first / mentions the 20.2.0 OSD crash-loop report when enabling it on a pool with ec_overwrites

evals.name: min-alloc-size-hdd
evals.prompt: Old runbook says to set bluestore_min_alloc_size_hdd=65536 on our HDD OSDs for better throughput with RGW. We're on Squid under Rook. Should I set that before adding new HDD OSDs, and can I change it on existing ones?
evals.expected_output: Default is 4K for HDD and SSD; the 64K advice is obsolete (space amplification for small objects); value fixed at OSD creation, changing requires redeploying the OSD.
assertions: States the current default bluestore_min_alloc_size_hdd is 4 KiB (4096)
Says the 64 KiB advice is obsolete / not recommended now
States the value is fixed at OSD creation and changing it requires redeploying (recreating) the OSD

evals.name: osd-memory-request-sizing
evals.prompt: Rook CephCluster: I set spec.resources.osd.limits.memory: 8Gi and requests.memory: 4Gi. What osd_memory_target will each OSD actually get, and is this a good setup for NVMe OSDs?
evals.expected_output: Request used 1:1 -> 4Gi target; limit only default when no request; leave headroom; NVMe benefits from more; verify with ceph config show.
assertions: States osd_memory_target will be 4Gi because the request is used 1:1
Explains the limit x 0.8 rule applies only when no request is set
Recommends verifying with ceph config show osd.N osd_memory_target

evals.name: pg-autoscaler-target
evals.prompt: Rook cluster, 24 OSDs, one big RBD pool holding ~90% of data plus a few small pools. The autoscaler gave the big pool only 128 PGs and I see uneven OSD usage. How should I configure the autoscaler instead of hand-setting pg_num?
evals.expected_output: Mark big pool bulk, set target_size_ratio, consider mon_target_pg_per_osd 200 (default 100, docs recommend 200).
assertions: Recommends setting the bulk flag on the large pool
Recommends setting target_size_ratio on the large pool
Mentions mon_target_pg_per_osd default 100 and that raising it (docs recommend 200) increases PGs per OSD

evals.name: rbd-cache-krbd
evals.prompt: Database on an RBD PVC via ceph-csi (default StorageClass from Rook). I want to tune librbd caching: disable write-back and raise readahead with rbd config pool set. Will that affect my PVC?
evals.expected_output: ceph-csi default mounter is krbd; librbd cache options don't apply to krbd; only rbd-nbd (alpha) uses librbd.
assertions: States ceph-csi mounts RBD PVCs with krbd (kernel RBD) by default
States librbd cache/readahead settings do not apply to krbd-mounted PVCs
Notes rbd-nbd would use librbd but is alpha / not recommended for production

evals.name: crimson-production
evals.prompt: Tentacle is out; is Crimson / SeaStore ready so we can deploy our new NVMe cluster on crimson-osd for lower latency?
evals.expected_output: No: tech preview, not suitable for production.
assertions: States Crimson is still a tech preview / not suitable for production in Tentacle
Does not recommend deploying production on crimson-osd or SeaStore

evals.name: rados-bench-method
evals.prompt: I want to benchmark our Ceph cluster's raw RADOS write then read throughput with rados bench, and then see what a real PVC gets. Give me the commands and the pitfalls.
evals.expected_output: rados bench write with --no-cleanup, then seq/rand, then cleanup; rbd bench bypasses kernel; fio in a pod with direct=1; multiple clients; dataset larger than cache.
assertions: Uses rados bench ... write --no-cleanup before the seq/rand read phases
Includes cleaning up the benchmark objects afterwards
Recommends fio inside a pod on the PVC (direct I/O) to measure the real client path
Mentions running multiple clients in parallel or a dataset larger than caches
